# Excellence 2026: Artificial Intelligence Solutions


October 29, 2026


by Craig Patton


##


Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from an experiment to a strategic priority across government. As public sector organizations look for ways to increase productivity, strengthen decision-making, and improve service delivery, the focus is shifting from whether to use AI to how to apply it responsibly to real challenges.


Government organizations are finding value by starting with practical, well-defined uses where results can be measured and people remain central to the work. From automating repetitive tasks to finding insights in complex data, AI can give public servants more time and information to focus on the work that matters most to their communities.


## Celebrating Excellence in Artificial Intelligence Solutions


For 2027, the[Tyler Excellence Awards](https://www.tylertech.com/about-us/tyler-client-difference/tyler-excellence-awards) are introducing an Artificial Intelligence category to recognize organizations using AI to advance the mission of government. While the category is new, Tyler clients were already demonstrating purposeful AI use in their 2026 award-winning stories across other categories. The examples below show how organizations are using AI to improve productivity, inform decisions, strengthen service delivery, and prepare for what’s next.


## Automating Invoice Processing to Give Staff Time Back


As accounts payable demands outgrew their small finance team’s bandwidth, the city of[Jacksonville, Texas](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/automation-cuts-invoice-processing-from-hours-to-minutes) , replaced paper-driven processes with ERP Pro’s AP Automation. The solution used AI-enabled invoice capture to streamline routing and strengthen controls without adding staff. Since implementation, the city has:


- Reduced invoice review time by 90%, freeing staff for higher-value work
- Eliminated duplicate payments to improve accuracy and audit readiness
- Streamlined check runs to ensure vendors receive payments on time


“By embedding accountability, documentation, and visibility directly into daily workflows, the city improved not only efficiency, but confidence — among departments, vendors, auditors, and leadership,” said Finance Director Roxanna Briley.


## Scaling AI Responsibly Across a Major Court System


Facing a sharp increase in e-filings and persistent resource constraints, the[Dallas County, Texas](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/dallas-county-proves-ai-can-work-responsibly-at-scale) , District and County Clerk’s Office turned to automation to address time-consuming and repetitive filing review tasks. By using AI-powered document processing, the court:


- Achieved greater filing consistency and staff productivity through fewer manual data entry tasks
- Processed more filings without affecting resources
- Shortened time to acceptance, allowing staff to focus on more strategic work


“We’re not replacing staff; we’re shifting their focus to work that requires judgment and direct involvement with justice,” said Ashley Arnold, court technology manager.


## Expanding Court Capacity With Always-On AI


[Fulton County, Georgia](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/vision-and-control-how-fulton-county-scaled-ai-across-courts) , sought to modernize its filing intake and review workflows. They aimed to create a court capable of delivering consistent, accurate, and timely service regardless of staffing levels or case volume. Under the leadership of Ché Alexander, the Clerk of Superior and Magistrate Courts, the county:


- Cleared case backlogs by scaling AI with guardrails, rules-based workflows, and leadership
- Reduced administrative work by 5-10% and time to acceptance by 8-12%
- Improved filing precision while retaining human oversight


“The system runs 24/7,” said Tim Ezell, chief deputy clerk and COO. “When you compare an eight-hour clerk day to continuous processing, the impact is clear.”


## Aligning Budget Decisions With Community Priorities


The city of[Liberty Lake, Washington](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/budget-process-optimized-for-flexibility-and-priorities) , modernized its budgeting process to align investments with strategic priorities. The city implemented AI-enabled Priority Based Budgeting to move beyond traditional line-item reviews with a community-driven framework. Adoption:


- Aligned budget investments with the city’s strategic plan
- Documented resource allocation using ROI reports and quadrant tools
- Evaluated new requests based on return on investment


“We wanted to convert to a process and a system that we knew was flexible enough and agile enough to allow us to adjust when times weren’t as great as they are now,” said Mark McAvoy, city administrator.


## Shaping AI Around the Mission of Probation


To reduce the time spent on routine administrative tasks that consumed officer workloads,[Placer County Probation, California](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/blog-articles/inside-placer-countys-decision-to-shape-ai-driven-probation) , turned to data insights and AI-driven community supervision. By embracing new AI technology, Placer County:


- Augmented administrative tasks through automated transcripts, summaries, and follow-up items
- Improved consistency, clarity, and confidence among officers
- Automated routine reporting such as presentence reports
- Protected access to sensitive client data


“Being an early partner gives us a voice in building tools that actually fit probation work,” said Nick Boone, senior deputy probation officer. “These efficiency gains will allow staff to take on more meaningful work.”


**More TEA Winners:** Explore the rest of the[2026 Tyler Excellence Award winners](https://www.tylertech.com/about-us/tyler-client-difference/tyler-excellence-awards/2026-winners) and their stories across every category. As applications open for 2027, the new Artificial Intelligence category will recognize organizations putting AI to work for government and the communities they serve.


**2026 Award Winner Categories:** Jacksonville, Texas — Operational Efficiency; Dallas County, Texas — Operational Efficiency; Fulton County, Georgia — Operational Efficiency; Liberty Lake, Washington — Performance & Innovation; Placer County, California — Performance & Innovation.
